learningObjective: Explain what AOTInductor produces (a self-contained shared library that runs a compiled PyTorch model without a Python runtime) and how that differs from torch.compile in JIT mode.

canonicalClaims.claim: AOTInductor takes a torch.export'd graph and ahead-of-time compiles it into a native shared library plus generated kernels. The resulting artifact runs without Python and without the Inductor compiler; JIT torch.compile compiles lazily and requires Python+Inductor at run time.
conditions: The model is torch.export-compatible (no unsupported dynamism).
nonImplications: Does not imply full feature parity with JIT torch.compile.
Does not imply zero build cost.

misconceptions.whyWrong: The artifact is a native shared library; no interpreter is embedded.
It calls into CUDA via generated kernels and standard driver APIs.
AOTInductor emits .so (or .dll) shared libraries and generated CUDA/Triton kernels.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor eliminates the need for torch.export.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AOTInductor operates on the output of torch.export.
